title: Adoption of Clean Architecture and Tiered Model Routing Abstraction
context_and_problem: The factory requires a modular architectural foundation that strictly separates application code from factory governance, while avoiding vendor lock-in to hardcoded foundation model identifiers.
decision_drivers: Maintain complete independence between core domain logic and third-party frameworks
Prevent brittle prompt failures by decoupling model routing into capability tiers (reasoning, standard, fast)
Guarantee that all factory policies reside inside .agentic/ without polluting root application directories

considered_options.option: Hardcoded model names with monolithic script architecture
cons: Brittle, provider lock-in, fails if model name deprecated, poor maintainability

considered_options.option: Clean Architecture with Tier-Based Provider Abstraction (.agentic/)
pros: High modularity, portable across Gemini/Claude/GPT, testable in isolation, clear boundary
cons: Requires formal schema definitions and abstraction layers

decision_outcome: Adopt Clean Architecture with Tier-Based Provider Abstraction. Encapsulate all factory intelligence inside .agentic/.

positive: Application source code remains clean and free of agent scaffolding
Model routing dynamically swaps providers with zero code modifications
negative: Initial configuration overhead requiring JSON schema validation
risks: Developers might mistakenly attempt to commit factory-owned configurations to root folders if unguided

validation: Automated factory validator (validate_factory.py) checks that all factory assets reside inside .agentic/ and pass schema validation.
